question: Should new or existing capital hold Intuitive Surgical after its Stage 4 break below $401.77, or do ex-SBC valuation math and 2027 pricing pressures require standing aside?

epigraph.quote: Dominant clinical platforms deserve lifelong study, yet disciplined capital enters only when ex-SBC cash-flow value and Stage 2 trend align.
epigraph.author: Investment Committee Summary

web_blocks.html: Intuitive Surgical (NASDAQ: ISRG) operates a premier COMPOUNDER_PASS surgical robotics franchise with 12,094 da Vinci systems, 1,152 Ion systems, newly cleared IG1000 GI tech (K253702), 84%–85% recurring revenue, 18.50% ROIC, and $6.80 billion in net cash [3, 4, 22, 34]. Yet a great business is not automatically a buy at every price or trend stage. On November 20, 2026, ISRG dropped 10.04% for the week to $399.05 (48.28x TTM GAAP P/E, 31.95x Forward P/E), slicing below our prior $401.77 stop into STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED) while facts_US_2026-11-20.json still shows Stage 1 (Basing) [22, 23].

Forensic Pass 1 and Pass 2 re-underwriting uncovered six material headwinds: (1) U.S. da Vinci growth slowing to ~10% YoY on low double-digit bariatric declines. Next, (2) U.S. Ion lung penetration crossing 50%. Third, (3) FDA authorizations for Medtronic Hugo (K250725) and J&J OTTAVA (DEN250068). Fourth, (4) -3% to -5% benign-case and China NHSA tool price cuts. Fifth, (5) the Ninth Circuit SIS antitrust reversal alongside a $450 million settlement. and (6) 0.9% ongoing tariff drag masked by $53.2 million in one-time IEEPA refunds plus uninspected Mexicali FDA risk and Class II dV5/SureForm recalls [3, 4, 28, 32, 33, 35]. Deducting $835.3 million in TTM pre-tax SBC and the unpaid $450.0 million settlement accrual from $3,598.5 million headline FCF leaves $2,313.2 million in normalized ex-SBC FCF (59.8x P/FCF) [3, 22]. Our SBC-adjusted 12-month Base Fair Value is $375.00 (-6.0% below CMP. PWV $358.50. Bull $465.00. Bear $260.00). Because even realistic Pivot S2 support ($345.25–$356.90) versus a $325.00 stop yields just 0.57:1 asymmetry, we assign REJECTED (TIER_0. VALUATION, TREND) for new capital, keep existing status at NOT_HELD (0 shares), and hold 100% CASH [23, 26].

book_subsections.title: The Case—and Why Discipline Says No at $399.05
paragraphs: Intuitive Surgical remains one of the finest medical technology platforms in public markets. By September 30, 2026, more than 12,094 da Vinci systems and 1,152 Ion lung-biopsy systems sit inside operating rooms worldwide, generating 84 to 85 percent recurring revenue and an 18.50 percent return on invested capital on a debt-free balance sheet holding $6.80 billion in cash and investments. Across ten years through 2025, revenue nearly quadrupled to $10.06 billion without a single annual operating loss.

Yet great businesses still become poor investments when price, margin headwinds, and technical structure turn against the buyer. On November 20, 2026, ISRG shares fell 10.04 percent for the week to $399.05, breaking straight through our prior $401.77 structural stop and closing below the 30-week average ($406.23), 50-day average ($423.51), and declining 200-day average ($427.69). While our market-facts ledger still tags Stage 1 Basing, our TradingView evaluation classifies ISRG as Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED), inside a 10-distribution-day S&P 500 Downtrend.

At the same time, Pass 1 and Pass 2 forensic checks lowered our intrinsic value estimate cleanly below today's market price. Stripping $835.3 million in trailing stock-based compensation and the unpaid $450.0 million antitrust accrual from $3,598.5 million in headline free cash flow reduces true normalized owner cash flow to $2,313.2 million—a steep 59.8 times multiple at $399.05. Meanwhile, Medtronic's Hugo and Johnson & Johnson's OTTAVA both won U.S. FDA authorizations in 2025–2026, management quantified -3 to -5 percent instrument price cuts in benign procedures and China, and 9M 2026 operating cash absorbed -$822.0 million into inventory and lease fleets.

book_subsections.title: The Verdict, Holding Action, and Watchlist Conditions
paragraphs: Blending 38.0 times FY2027 GAAP EPS of $9.77 with our 10-year ex-SBC DCF puts 12-month Base Fair Value at $375.00 per share, alongside a $465.00 Bull Case, a $260.00 Bear Case, and a probability-weighted value of $358.50 (-10.2 percent below CMP). Even if shares pull back to realistic Stage 4 support at Pivot S2 ($345.25 to $356.90) backed by a genuine 2.21x ATR stop at $325.00, upside to $375.00 offers only 0.57-to-1 asymmetry—well short of our 1.50-to-1 hurdle.

Accordingly, we assign REJECTED (TIER_0; VALUATION and TREND) for new capital rather than hedging with wait-for-support. Inside the portfolio, ISRG is NOT_HELD (0 shares across Schwab and Robinhood), and 100 percent of incremental cash stays liquid at 4.76 to 5.04 percent ahead of Stage 2 peers AbbVie and Stryker while portfolio cash sits at just 3.38 percent of net worth. We revisit ISRG only after a durable Stage 1 base reclaims the 200-day average or a deep market flush below $315.00 restores 1.50-to-1 asymmetry.
